rules.title: SharpDX assembly reference
rules.explanation: The project references SharpDX assemblies (SharpDX, SharpDX.Toolkit.*, SharpDX.Direct3D11 and others). They come from the SharpDX 2.x NuGet packages, which target .NET Framework 4.x and need the SharpDX build targets. They are not part of MonoGame.
rules.resolution: The migrator writes an SDK-style project that drops every SharpDX reference and references MonoGame instead. Code that used SharpDX types directly is reported by the SDX005 to SDX008 and SDX034 to SDX035 rules.

rules.title: SharpDX build targets import
rules.explanation: The project imports SharpDX.targets or SharpDX.Toolkit.targets from the NuGet packages folder. Those files set the reference paths and run the Toolkit content compilers. They exist only after a NuGet restore of the old packages, and a build without them stops with MSB4019.
rules.resolution: The migrator drops the imports, the NuGet restore guard target and the import stamp from the SDK-style project it writes.

rules.title: .NET Framework 4.x target
rules.explanation: The project targets .NET Framework 4.x (for example v4.5). MonoGame 3.8.6.1 desktop projects target net8.0.
rules.resolution: The migrator writes an SDK-style project for net8.0 (or the Windows variant for WindowsDX).

rules.title: Windows Store or Windows Phone project
rules.explanation: The project type GUIDs include the Windows Store app type (BC8A1FFA), the Windows Phone 8 type (C089C8C0), the Windows Phone 8.1 type (76F1466A) or the Universal Windows type (A5A43C5B). The first two are the non-desktop project types of the Toolkit project template (read from ProjectTemplate.csproj in the Toolkit repository). The last two were found on real Toolkit projects. MonoGame desktop cannot host any of them.
rules.resolution: Migrate the game code into a desktop Toolkit project first, or port it by hand. XNA Reborn refuses these projects and creates no copy for them.

rules.title: Direct use of SharpDX.Direct3D11
rules.explanation: The code uses the raw Direct3D 11 API through SharpDX.Direct3D11. MonoGame has no such layer. Code written against devices, contexts and buffers has to be rewritten against the MonoGame graphics API. Matching is by syntax only, so a look-alike name in unrelated code can match.
rules.resolution: Rewrite the affected code with MonoGame GraphicsDevice, VertexBuffer, IndexBuffer and Effect types. This cannot be automated.

rules.title: Direct use of SharpDX.DXGI
rules.explanation: The code uses SharpDX.DXGI, usually for pixel formats and swap chain settings. Formats map to MonoGame SurfaceFormat in simple cases, but not by name. Matching is by syntax only, so a look-alike name in unrelated code can match.
rules.resolution: Replace each DXGI format or setting with the MonoGame equivalent (SurfaceFormat, PresentationParameters) by hand.

rules.title: Direct use of SharpDX.Direct2D1
rules.explanation: The code draws with Direct2D through SharpDX.Direct2D1. MonoGame has no Direct2D layer. Matching is by syntax only, so a look-alike name in unrelated code can match.
rules.resolution: Redraw the content with SpriteBatch or a render target. This cannot be automated.

rules.title: Direct use of SharpDX.XAudio2
rules.explanation: The code plays audio through SharpDX.XAudio2. MonoGame offers SoundEffect, SoundEffectInstance and Song instead. Matching is by syntax only, so a look-alike name in unrelated code can match.
rules.resolution: Replace the XAudio2 calls with SoundEffect and SoundEffectInstance. This cannot be automated.

rules.title: Toolkit font (ToolkitFont)
rules.explanation: The project builds fonts with the ToolkitFont build action. The source is a TkFont XML file that the Toolkit compiles to .tkb. MonoGame cannot read .tkb files and uses .spritefont files instead.
rules.resolution: The migrator converts each TkFont file to a .spritefont file and adds it to Content.mgcb. Line spacing and premultiply settings have no MonoGame field and are listed in the content report.

rules.title: Toolkit texture (ToolkitTexture)
rules.explanation: The project builds textures with the ToolkitTexture build action. The Toolkit mostly copies the image into a .tkb file. MonoGame loads textures built by the content pipeline.
rules.resolution: The migrator adds each texture whose format the MonoGame builder accepts to Content.mgcb. Other formats are listed as manual work in the content report.

rules.title: Toolkit model (ToolkitModel)
rules.explanation: The project builds models with the ToolkitModel build action (the tkmodel compiler, based on Assimp). The result is a .tkb file that MonoGame cannot read.
rules.resolution: The migrator adds each FBX or X model to Content.mgcb with the model importer. Other formats are listed as manual work. The loaded Model type differs from the Toolkit one (see SDX047).

rules.title: Toolkit effect (ToolkitFxc)
rules.explanation: The project builds effects with the ToolkitFxc build action (the tkfxc compiler). Toolkit effects use a syntax that the MonoGame effect compiler rejects. Checked with the compiler of dotnet-mgcb 3.8.6.1: a pass that names its shader without the compile keyword (PixelShader = Name;) fails with "Unexpected token 'P' found. Expected Compile"; a Profile = 9.1; pass state fails with "Unexpected token 'P' found. Expected CloseBracket"; a Direct3D 10 sampler block (Filter = MIN_MAG_MIP_POINT;) fails with "Unexpected token 'M' found. Expected None, Linear, Point, or Anisotropic." Texture2D<float4> declarations parse. The Toolkit can also generate wrapper classes that are not in source control.
rules.resolution: Rewrite each .fx file in the MonoGame effect syntax by hand and add it to Content.mgcb. The migrator copies the original and flags it. Code that used a generated wrapper class needs the wrapper removed.

rules.title: Toolkit audio (ToolkitAudio)
rules.explanation: The project builds sounds with the ToolkitAudio build action. The result is a .tkb file that MonoGame cannot read.
rules.resolution: The migrator adds each .wav file to Content.mgcb with the sound effect processor. Other audio formats are listed as manual work.

rules.title: Prebuilt .tkb asset
rules.explanation: The project folder holds compiled .tkb files. When the source asset is not in the folder, nothing can rebuild the asset for MonoGame, and MonoGame has no importer for the .tkb format.
rules.resolution: Find the original image, font, model or sound and add it to the project, or leave the asset out. The migrator copies .tkb files unchanged and flags them.

rules.title: Toolkit game namespace
rules.explanation: The code imports SharpDX.Toolkit, which holds Game, GameTime and GraphicsDeviceManager. The same names live in Microsoft.Xna.Framework in MonoGame. Matching is by syntax only, so a look-alike name in unrelated code can match.
rules.resolution: The migrator rewrites the using directive to Microsoft.Xna.Framework.

rules.title: Toolkit graphics namespace
rules.explanation: The code imports SharpDX.Toolkit.Graphics (SpriteBatch, Texture2D, SpriteFont, BasicEffect). MonoGame keeps these names in Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Graphics. Matching is by syntax only, so a look-alike name in unrelated code can match.
rules.resolution: The migrator rewrites the using directive to Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Graphics.

rules.title: Toolkit content namespace
rules.explanation: The code imports SharpDX.Toolkit.Content (ContentManager). MonoGame has it in Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Content. Content.Load<T>(name) keeps its shape. Matching is by syntax only, so a look-alike name in unrelated code can match.
rules.resolution: The migrator rewrites the using directive to Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Content.

rules.title: SharpDX math namespace
rules.explanation: The code imports SharpDX for its math types (Vector2, Vector3, Matrix, Color, Rectangle). MonoGame keeps these names in Microsoft.Xna.Framework. Types that exist only in SharpDX are reported by SDX034 and SDX035. Matching is by syntax only, so a look-alike name in unrelated code can match.
rules.resolution: The migrator rewrites the using directive to Microsoft.Xna.Framework.

rules.title: Toolkit input namespace
rules.explanation: The code imports SharpDX.Toolkit.Input (Keys, KeyboardState, MouseManager). MonoGame has Keys and KeyboardState in Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Input. Matching is by syntax only, so a look-alike name in unrelated code can match.
rules.resolution: The migrator rewrites the using directive to Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Input.

rules.title: KeyboardManager
rules.explanation: The game creates a KeyboardManager and reads keys from it. MonoGame has the static Keyboard.GetState() and needs no manager. Matching is by syntax only, so a look-alike name in unrelated code can match.
rules.resolution: The migrator removes the manager field and its construction and replaces GetState() on it with Keyboard.GetState(). When the manager is used in any other way the code is left alone and marked.

rules.title: MouseManager
rules.explanation: The game uses MouseManager. MonoGame has the static Mouse class. The units of the Toolkit MouseState coordinates were not confirmed, so the call is not rewritten. Matching is by syntax only, so a look-alike name in unrelated code can match.
rules.resolution: Replace the manager with Mouse.GetState() and check the coordinates against the window size.

rules.title: PointerManager (touch)
rules.explanation: The game uses PointerManager for touch and pointer input. MonoGame uses TouchPanel with a different event model. Matching is by syntax only, so a look-alike name in unrelated code can match.
rules.resolution: Port the input code to TouchPanel or Mouse by hand.

rules.title: Edge-triggered key state
rules.explanation: The Toolkit KeyboardState tracks key edges (IsKeyPressed, IsKeyReleased). MonoGame does not: the game has to keep the previous state itself. Matching is by syntax only, so a look-alike name in unrelated code can match.
rules.resolution: Keep the previous KeyboardState in a field and compare it with the current one.

rules.title: Right-handed Matrix factories
rules.explanation: The code builds matrices with the SharpDX factory methods. The right-handed ones map to Matrix.Create* in MonoGame, which is also right-handed. Only calls on the type name Matrix match, not calls on a variable. Matching is by syntax only, so a look-alike name in unrelated code can match.
rules.resolution: The migrator renames the calls (LookAtRH to CreateLookAt, PerspectiveFovRH to CreatePerspectiveFieldOfView, Scaling to CreateScale and so on).

rules.title: MathUtil members
rules.explanation: The code uses SharpDX MathUtil. MonoGame has the same helpers on MathHelper, some under other names (PiOver2, PiOver4, ToRadians, ToDegrees). Matching is by syntax only, so a look-alike name in unrelated code can match.
rules.resolution: The migrator rewrites MathUtil.X to MathHelper.X and renames the members that differ.

rules.title: Left-handed Matrix factories
rules.explanation: The code builds left-handed matrices. XNA and MonoGame are right-handed. A rename would be wrong, because winding order and view direction change with the handedness. Matching is by syntax only, so a look-alike name in unrelated code can match.
rules.resolution: Convert the scene to right-handed coordinates (flip Z and the triangle winding), then use the Create* factories.

rules.title: Vector3.TransformCoordinate
rules.explanation: TransformCoordinate divides by w. MonoGame Vector3.Transform does not. The result is the same for affine matrices and different for projection matrices. Matching is by syntax only, so a look-alike name in unrelated code can match.
rules.resolution: Use Vector3.Transform for affine matrices. For a projection, transform as Vector4 and divide by w.

rules.title: RectangleF
rules.explanation: RectangleF is a SharpDX type with float fields. MonoGame has no such type, and SpriteBatch.Draw takes a Rectangle with integer fields. Matching is by syntax only, so a look-alike name in unrelated code can match.
rules.resolution: Use Rectangle, or add a small struct of your own. With the compatibility shims on, the migrated copy gets a RectangleF stand-in (sharpdx-toolkit task 14) and no marker.

rules.title: Color4 and Color3
rules.explanation: Color4 and Color3 are float color structs of SharpDX. MonoGame has Color (bytes) and Vector4 (floats) but no type of this name. Matching is by syntax only, so a look-alike name in unrelated code can match.
rules.resolution: Use Color for byte colors or Vector4 for float colors. With the compatibility shims on, the migrated copy gets Color4 and Color3 stand-ins (sharpdx-toolkit task 14) and no marker.

rules.title: Graphics state collections
rules.explanation: The code reads states from GraphicsDevice.BlendStates, SamplerStates, DepthStencilStates or RasterizerStates. MonoGame has static BlendState, SamplerState and DepthStencilState members. Names that do not map one to one (BlendStates.Default, RasterizerStates.*, SamplerStates.Default) are marked, not renamed. Face culling may look inverted after a change of handedness. Matching is by syntax only, so a look-alike name in unrelated code can match.
rules.resolution: The migrator rewrites GraphicsDevice.BlendStates.X to BlendState.X and does the same for samplers and depth states. Names without an equivalent get a marker.

rules.title: Set*State calls
rules.explanation: The code sets a state with GraphicsDevice.SetBlendState(state) and its relatives. MonoGame uses properties on the device. Matching is by syntax only, so a look-alike name in unrelated code can match.
rules.resolution: The migrator rewrites the one-argument call to an assignment (GraphicsDevice.BlendState = state).

rules.title: SetRenderTargets (one target)
rules.explanation: The code sets one render target with SetRenderTargets(target). MonoGame calls this SetRenderTarget. Matching is by syntax only, so a look-alike name in unrelated code can match.
rules.resolution: The migrator renames the call to SetRenderTarget.

rules.title: SetRenderTargets (depth buffer or several targets)
rules.explanation: The code passes a depth buffer or several targets to SetRenderTargets. In MonoGame a render target owns its depth buffer, and several targets are set with SetRenderTargets(RenderTargetBinding[]). Matching is by syntax only, so a look-alike name in unrelated code can match.
rules.resolution: Create each render target with the depth format it needs and set them with SetRenderTargets(params RenderTargetBinding[]).

rules.title: BackBuffer size
rules.explanation: The code reads GraphicsDevice.BackBuffer, usually for its Width and Height. MonoGame keeps the size in PresentationParameters. Uses other than Width and Height are marked. Matching is by syntax only, so a look-alike name in unrelated code can match.
rules.resolution: The migrator rewrites GraphicsDevice.BackBuffer.Width to GraphicsDevice.PresentationParameters.BackBufferWidth (and the same for Height).

rules.title: RenderTarget2D.New
rules.explanation: RenderTarget2D.New is a static factory that takes a DXGI PixelFormat and a mip map count. MonoGame uses a constructor with SurfaceFormat and DepthFormat. Matching is by syntax only, so a look-alike name in unrelated code can match.
rules.resolution: Call new RenderTarget2D(device, width, height, mipMap, SurfaceFormat.Color, DepthFormat.Depth24) and pick the formats by hand.

rules.title: Texture2D.New
rules.explanation: Texture2D.New is a static factory that takes a DXGI PixelFormat. MonoGame uses new Texture2D(device, width, height) with a SurfaceFormat. Matching is by syntax only, so a look-alike name in unrelated code can match.
rules.resolution: Use the Texture2D constructor and set the pixels with SetData.

rules.title: Toolkit Model API
rules.explanation: The Toolkit Model draws itself with Model.Draw(device, world, view, projection) and owns its effects differently from the MonoGame Model. Matching is by syntax only, so a look-alike name in unrelated code can match.
rules.resolution: Draw each mesh with its effect by hand, the way MonoGame samples do.

rules.title: GeometricPrimitive
rules.explanation: GeometricPrimitive (cube, sphere, teapot and so on) has no MonoGame equivalent. Matching is by syntax only, so a look-alike name in unrelated code can match.
rules.resolution: Build the vertex and index buffers yourself, or load a model for the shape.

rules.title: Effect parameter SetResource
rules.explanation: SetResource sets a texture or sampler on an effect parameter. MonoGame sets textures with SetValue(Texture) and sets samplers on the device. Matching is by syntax only, so a look-alike name in unrelated code can match.
rules.resolution: Use EffectParameter.SetValue(texture) and GraphicsDevice.SamplerStates.

rules.title: DrawQuad
rules.explanation: GraphicsDevice.DrawQuad draws a full-screen quad. MonoGame has no such call. Matching is by syntax only, so a look-alike name in unrelated code can match.
rules.resolution: Draw a full-screen SpriteBatch pass instead.

rules.title: SpriteBatch.Begin(sortMode, effect)
rules.explanation: The Toolkit has a Begin(SpriteSortMode, Effect) overload that XNA and MonoGame lack. The rule looks for any two-argument call on a variable named spriteBatch, so it also finds Begin(SpriteSortMode, BlendState), which MonoGame accepts. It misses a SpriteBatch field with another name. Matching is by syntax only.
rules.resolution: Pass the effect in the long overload: Begin(sortMode, blendState, samplerState, depthStencilState, rasterizerState, effect).

rules.title: ToDisposeContent
rules.explanation: ToDisposeContent(x) registers x for disposal when the game unloads and returns x. MonoGame Game has no such method. Removing the call drops that automatic disposal. That changes nothing visible for objects that live as long as the game. The rule uses the type match because the call is normally a bare call of an inherited method. Matching is by syntax only, so a look-alike name in unrelated code can match.
rules.resolution: The migrator replaces ToDisposeContent(x) with x. Dispose objects that must not outlive their use in UnloadContent.

rules.title: PreferredGraphicsProfile
rules.explanation: The game asks for Direct3D feature levels with PreferredGraphicsProfile. MonoGame has GraphicsProfile.Reach and HiDef. Matching is by syntax only, so a look-alike name in unrelated code can match.
rules.resolution: Set GraphicsDeviceManager.GraphicsProfile to Reach or HiDef.

rules.title: GameSystem components
rules.explanation: GameSystem and its collection are the Toolkit game component model. MonoGame has GameComponent and DrawableGameComponent with a different lifecycle. Matching is by syntax only, so a look-alike name in unrelated code can match.
rules.resolution: Port each system to GameComponent or DrawableGameComponent.

rules.title: Hosted game (SharpDXElement)
rules.explanation: The game is hosted inside another UI (a WPF SharpDXElement or a WinRT game context). A MonoGame desktop game owns its window. Matching is by syntax only, so a look-alike name in unrelated code can match.
rules.resolution: Run the game in its own window and move the surrounding UI out of the game.
